title: Describe a person you know who dresses in an interesting way.
explain: and explain why their style makes such an impression on you.
followUps: Have you ever asked this person where they buy their clothes?
p3Topics: Dress codes at work and events
p3: Why do some people feel more confident when they wear something unusual?
How does wearing a uniform compare with choosing one's own clothes in the way people behave?
What effect can bold or unusual clothing have on how strangers treat someone?
What kinds of events still expect guests to follow a particular dress code?
What are the advantages of relaxed dress codes in offices compared with strict ones?
What might be gained and what might be lost if dress codes at work disappeared altogether?

title: Describe a person you know who has travelled to many countries.
explain: and explain how these trips have changed the way they see the world.
followUps: Would you like to visit some of those places yourself?
p3Topics: Travel as a way of learning
p3: What do people usually gain from spending time in another country?
How does travelling abroad compare with learning about a country from books?
What are the main advantages of one long trip compared with several short holidays?
How important is it for young people to see other countries before they settle down?
Will people in future travel as much as they do now, or will they stay closer to home?
How has cheap air travel changed the way families spend their holidays?

title: Describe a person who encouraged you to keep going.
bullets: what they said or did to help you
explain: and explain why their support mattered so much at the time.
followUps: Have you ever thanked this person properly?
p3: What kinds of encouragement do children respond to best?
How do the ways teachers encourage pupils differ from the ways parents do?
What makes some people give up on a goal more easily than others?
What qualities make an experienced colleague a good mentor for a newcomer?
How much can a mentor at work affect a young person's career?
In what ways might the people who support us change as our lives develop?

title: Describe a theme park or funfair you went to.
bullets: which rides or attractions you enjoyed most
explain: and explain whether you would like to go back there.
followUps: Do you prefer fairs or big theme parks?
p3: What kinds of day out do families with young children tend to enjoy most?
How do outdoor fairs compare with indoor entertainment centres for a family outing?

What makes some amusement parks far more expensive to visit than others?
How might the way people spend their leisure time change over the next twenty years?
What effect could new technology have on the amusement parks of the future?

title: Describe a square or public space where people gather.
bullets: who you have seen using it
explain: and explain how this space brings the community together.
followUps: How often do you visit such places?
p3: What makes a public square feel welcoming to people of different ages?
Which is more valuable to a town, a busy square or a quiet park?
What separates a square that draws crowds from one that stays almost empty?
How far can a well-designed square change the way neighbours interact with each other?
Would a town with fewer public spaces lose something important, even if it gained more private homes?
How might public spaces be designed differently as cities grow more crowded?

title: Describe a place where children like to play near you.
explain: and explain why you think children enjoy this spot so much.
followUps: Did you play outside much when you were small?
p3: What kinds of games do children most often play outdoors?
How does playing outside differ from playing indoors for a young child?
What keeps many children indoors on screens rather than playing outside?
Is it always safe for children to play in public places without an adult nearby?
What might happen to childhood in cities if there are fewer open spaces to play in?
How have the places where children play changed over the last fifty years?

title: Describe a piece of sports equipment you own or have used.
explain: and explain why this item is important to you.
followUps: Would you recommend this equipment to a friend?
p3Topics: Sport and the cost of living
p3: What kinds of sports equipment do people spend the most money on?
How does the price of good equipment affect who can take part in a sport?
What leads some people to buy expensive kit even when they rarely play?
Would sharing equipment between local clubs make sport more accessible to more people?
How important is good equipment compared with regular training for an athlete's success?
How might sports equipment change over the next few decades?

title: Describe a box or container where you keep things that matter to you.
bullets: what sort of things you store inside
explain: and explain how you feel when you look through its contents.
followUps: Did you buy this box, or was it given to you?

How has the growth of digital photos changed the way families keep memories?

title: Describe a decoration you put up for a festival or celebration.
bullets: how it was made or bought
explain: and explain what the decoration meant to you.

title: Describe a community event in your area.
explain: and explain why local people enjoyed taking part.

title: Describe a dinner party you hosted or went to.

What role do shared meals play in helping people build friendships in a new community?

title: Describe a time when someone praised you.
bullets: how you reacted at the time

title: Describe a time when you were proud of yourself.
explain: and explain why this achievement still means a lot to you.

title: Describe a night when you could not sleep.

explain: and explain how you felt the next day.

title: Describe a club or group you belong to or would like to join.
